Notes on iPhone, to iOS 6

Apple’s iPhone notes app as a yellow ruled pad with a leather top and handwriting-style type, used until 2013.

Source
Wikipedia: Notes (Apple)
Creator
Apple
Made
Until 2013 (Wikipedia); the Mac version followed in OS X Mountain Lion (2012)
Style
Skeuomorphism (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Familiar, casual, tactile
Evidence
Based on Wikipedia and NN/g. The NN/g article shows an image of the early iOS notepad, but it was not saved or measured here.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

“Until 2013, both applications used a strongly skeuomorphic interface, with a lined, textured paper design; the Mountain Lion version placed this inside a leather folder.” Notes could use three fonts: Noteworthy, Marker Felt, and Helvetica. Wikipedia: Notes (Apple)).

NN/g: “This early iOS notepad design mimics a traditional paper notepad with textured lines and leather binding.” NN/g: Skeuomorphism.

Why it belongs

The handwriting face is part of the metaphor. The style record keeps it to places where the object would carry handwriting.

What to review next

  • Inspect a large screenshot of iOS 6 Notes and record the paper color and rule spacing.
